We're starting renewal discussions for BrightCart and want to align the term structure with our product roadmap. Hi Samira — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. We've reviewed the forecast and sketched two complementary paths that address predictability and burst flexibility. Attached is a high-level proposal (Redwood_Proposed_SLA_v2.pdf) and a one-pager MA plan summary. Key points: 

1) Blended-tenor 24/36 option: a 24-month commitment with a 36-month price ladder option — locks a lower unit rate if BrightCart extends to 36 months at the 12-month mark. This gives procurement predictable unit economics and an early optionality window.

2) Staged commit (graded ramp): year 1 commit at 70% of forecast, year 2 increases to 100% with quarterly true-ups. This reduces upfront cost while matching your growth profile.

3) Burst/top-up model: pre-purchased burst credits redeemable during campaign windows (discount relative to on-demand) + an emergency burst capacity pool (short-term reserved G-reserves) with a capped number of burst hours/month.

4) Auto-renew and break clause: auto-renew by default with a 60-day opt-out; a usage-safety valve allows either party to renegotiate if monthly usage exceeds 140% of committed run-rate for two consecutive months.

Next steps: Marissa and I can run expected unit economics for the three ramp trajectories you provided; Karthik can validate latency/SLAs for burst handling. If that sounds right, we'll send a versioned MA plan and sample contract language for Len.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Quick ops note: we can model a burst pool that we draw from for campaign windows; operationally we'd set a hard cap per campaign (e.g., 72 hours at 2x baseline) and a regeneration period. Two operational caveats: 
- KV cold-starts: for model variants with large KV state, recovery to steady latency could take ~10-30 minutes depending on sequence lengths; we can mitigate with pre-warming hooks.
- Billing of burst: recommended approach is prepaid burst credits (discounted) + pay-as-you-go overflow. We should reflect these as distinct line items in the MA appendix to keep invoice clarity.
